# 令 — command; decree

**Strokes:** 5 · **Key (radical):** 人 (no. 9) · **JLPT:** N2 (community list)

## Meaning and origin

令 concerns an order, command, or decree. 命令 めいれい is a command. Other compounds use a respectful or favorable sense, as in 令嬢 れいじょう, someone's daughter in respectful language; they should not be translated mechanically as commands.

**Modern-shape mnemonic, not etymology:** Imagine an instruction being issued from under the roof-like top and passed down through the lower strokes.

The indexing radical 人 is the two-stroke roof-like shape at the top, rather than its left-hand variant 亻.

## Readings

| Reading | Type | Typical words |
| --- | --- | --- |
| レイ | on | [命令](../words/命令.md) めいれい - command; order |

## Common words

- [命令](../words/命令.md) めいれい - command; order
- 法令 ほうれい - laws and regulations
- 令嬢 れいじょう - someone's daughter; a young lady

## Notes

- Compare 令 and [今](今.md) いま, now: pay attention to the extra strokes in 令's lower part rather than treating the roof-like tops as enough to identify them.
- The respectful use in 令嬢 does not make every 令 compound polite language.

# 命 — life; command

**Strokes:** 8 · **Key (radical):** 口 (no. 30) · **JLPT:** N3 (community list)

## Meaning and origin

命 has two important meanings to keep separate: life and a command.
The standalone noun [命](../words/命.md) いのち is life as something that can be protected or lost. 命令 めいれい means an order, not a kind of living.

**Modern-shape mnemonic:** the broad top shelters the small 口 below, as if protecting a life. This is only a memory image; it does not explain the historical connection between the meanings.

## Readings

| Reading | Type | Typical words |
| --- | --- | --- |
| いのち | kun | [命](../words/命.md) いのち — life |
| メイ | on | 命令 めいれい — order; command |
| ミョウ | on | 寿命 じゅみょう — lifespan |

## Common words

- [命](../words/命.md) いのち — life; life force
- 命令 めいれい — command
- 寿命 じゅみょう — lifespan; useful life of an object

## Notes

[会](会.md) and [今](今.md) share a broad upper outline with 命; look for the separate small box and the lower-right strokes.
[生活](../words/生活.md) せいかつ concerns living and one's daily life. It is not interchangeable with 命 in "save a life."

# 束 — bundle

**Strokes:** 7 · **Key (radical):** 木 (no. 75) · **JLPT:** N3 (community list)

## Meaning and origin

束 gathers separate things into a bundle. The noun 束 (たば) can describe a bunch of flowers or a bundle of papers.
In [約束](../words/約束.md) (やくそく), the whole word means a promise or agreement, not a physical bundle.

**Modern-shape mnemonic:** imagine the central upright and spreading lower strokes tied together by the square in the middle.
This is a memory picture, not a historical derivation.

## Readings

The table selects useful readings; the metadata also preserves つか and つか.ねる.

| Reading | Type | Typical words |
| --- | --- | --- |
| たば | kun | 束 たば — bundle |
| たば.ねる | kun | 束ねる たばねる — tie into a bundle |
| ソク | on | [約束](../words/約束.md) やくそく — promise |

## Common words

- [約束](../words/約束.md) やくそく — promise; agreement
- 束 たば — bundle; bunch
- 束ねる たばねる — bundle together; also manage a group

## Notes

[東](東.md) has a divided central enclosure; 束 has the simpler 口-like square.
束ねる is transitive: 花を束ねる (はなをたばねる), "tie flowers into a bunch."
The management sense extends beyond physically tying things.

# 効 — efficacy; effectiveness

**Strokes:** 8 · **Key (radical):** 力 (no. 19) · **JLPT:** N2 (community list)

## Meaning and origin

効 concerns effectiveness or an effect. 効く きく means to work effectively or take effect, while 効果 こうか names an effect. 有効 ゆうこう can mean effective or valid, depending on the thing being described.

**Modern-shape mnemonic, not etymology:** Picture the crossing 交 shape beside 力, strength, as though effort is producing an effective result.

The canonical radical 力 is the right-hand component.

## Readings

| Reading | Type | Typical words |
| --- | --- | --- |
| コウ | on | [効果](../words/効果.md) こうか - effect; effectiveness |
| き.く | kun | [効く](../words/効く.md) きく - take effect; be effective |
| ききめ | kun | Source-only reading; see the qualification below. |
| なら.う | kun | Source-only reading; see the qualification below. |

KANJIDIC2 also records `ききめ`, `なら.う`. No suitable word example was established in the inspected JMdict snapshot. These are character-dictionary readings for lookup, not recommendations to use this kanji as an everyday spelling of a word.

## Common words

- [効く](../words/効く.md) きく - take effect; be effective
- [効果](../words/効果.md) こうか - effect; effectiveness
- [効力](../words/効力.md) こうりょく - efficacy; validity; potency
- [有効](../words/有効.md) ゆうこう - effective; valid

## Notes

- 効く is intransitive: 薬が効く くすりがきく means a medicine works. Its shared dictionary entry also includes 利く in expressions about faculties or senses; spelling choices belong to whole expressions.
- The ordinary word 効き目 ききめ means effectiveness. Its written き and separate 目 do not establish that 効 alone normally spells the whole reading ききめ. The source-only ききめ and ならう rows are retained for character-dictionary lookup.

勤 appears in words about employment, service, and diligent activity.
[勤める](../words/勤める.md) つとめる describes working for an employer;
通勤 つうきん is the journey to work.

**Modern-shape mnemonic:** think of 力 reporting for work beside the densely stacked left side.

# 訓 — instruction; kun reading

**Strokes:** 10 · **Key (radical):** 言 (no. 149) · **JLPT:** N2 (community list)

## Meaning and origin

訓 concerns instruction, precepts and explaining or reading written characters. It also names a native Japanese kanji reading, a 訓 くん, in contrast with an on reading.

**Modern-shape mnemonic, not etymology:** Imagine a teacher's words 言 flowing clearly like the right-hand 川, a river. This is a memory aid, not an assertion that either component had that historical role.

## Readings

| Reading | Type | Typical words |
| --- | --- | --- |
| クン | on | [訓練](../words/訓練.md) くんれん - training; drill |
| キン | on | 家訓 かきん - family precepts; family motto |
| おし.える | kun | Source-only reading. JMdict indexes 訓える おしえる - teach; instruct (search-only kanji form); this index form is not a recommended word example. |
| よ.む | kun | Source-only reading. JMdict indexes 訓む よむ - read with a native Japanese reading (search-only kanji form); this index form is not a recommended word example. |
| くん.ずる | kun | 訓ずる くんずる - read kanji using its native Japanese pronunciation (rare word/use) |

KANJIDIC2 records おし.える and よ.む. JMdict retains 訓える and 訓む as search-only kanji forms: the rows above are explicitly index evidence, not ordinary recommended spellings. For the teaching word, use 教える おしえる; 読む よむ is the non-index reading spelling in its family. The specific 訓む sense concerns reading a kanji with its native Japanese reading, not a recommendation to respell every occurrence of 読む.

## Common words

- [訓](../words/訓.md) くん - native Japanese kanji reading
- [訓練](../words/訓練.md) くんれん - training; drill

## Notes

- The キン row uses the attested 家訓 かきん. The same entry also has かくん; dictionary order or a missing frequency flag does not by itself establish how frequent either reading is.
- JMdict marks 訓ずる くんずる as a rare term. It illustrates the source reading without making it an everyday verb recommendation.
- The noun 訓 くん uses an on reading even though it names the kun-reading category. A word's meaning does not determine whether its own pronunciation is on or kun.

# 法 — law; method

**Strokes:** 8 · **Key (radical):** 水 (as 氵, no. 85) · **JLPT:** N3 (community list)

## Meaning and origin

法 can concern a rule that governs conduct or a method for doing something.
[方法](../words/方法.md) ほうほう is a method; 法律 (ほうりつ) is law.
The shared character does not make an ordinary method a legal requirement.

**Modern-shape mnemonic:** combine the visible water strokes with [去](去.md), "leave":
an orderly method makes a mess go away. This is not an account of the character's origin.

## Readings

| Reading | Type | Typical words |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ホウ | on | [方法](../words/方法.md) ほうほう — method; 法律 ほうりつ — law |

The compound 文法 is ぶんぽう, with ぽう rather than a separately pronounced ほう.
The front matter preserves the additional dictionary readings; this table selects the useful ホウ family.

## Common words

- [方法](../words/方法.md) ほうほう — method; way of doing something
- 法律 ほうりつ — law; legislation
- 文法 ぶんぽう — grammar

## Notes

この方法でやります。 (このほうほうでやります。) — I will do it using this method.
Here で marks the method used. Visually, keep the lower 厶-shaped part of 去 separate from
the lower legs in [洗](洗.md) and the spreading right side of [泳](泳.md).

# 教 — teach, instruct

**Strokes:** 11 · **Key (radical):** 攴 (right-side shape 攵, no. 66) · **JLPT:** N4 (community list)

## Meaning and origin

教 concerns teaching and instruction; in some compounds it also concerns a doctrine or faith. The everyday verb 教える includes telling someone information, not just teaching a lesson.

**Modern-shape mnemonic:** notice [子](子.md) within the left side and picture a child following a teacher's pointing gesture on the right. This is an invented memory scene, not a claim about the origin of 攵.

## Readings

| Reading | Type | Typical words |
| --- | --- | --- |
| キョウ | on | [教室](../words/教室.md) きょうしつ (classroom), 教科書 きょうかしょ (textbook) |
| おし.える | kun | [教える](../words/教える.md) おしえる (teach; tell) |
| おそ.わる | kun | 教わる おそわる (be taught; learn from someone) |

## Common words

- [教える](../words/教える.md) おしえる — teach; tell someone information
- 教わる おそわる — be taught, learn from someone
- [教室](../words/教室.md) きょうしつ — classroom
- 教科書 きょうかしょ — textbook
- [儒教](../words/儒教.md) じゅきょう — Confucianism
- [准教授](../words/准教授.md) じゅんきょうじゅ — associate professor

教える views the exchange from the instructor's side; 教わる views it from the learner's side. The verb is not limited to school: a person can 教える a name or an address.

# 命令 (めいれい) - order; command

## Meaning

命令 is a noun for an order or command. 命令する means "order someone to do something."
A useful pattern is person + に + plain nonpast verb + ように命令する.

- 上司は部下に待つように命令しました。 (じょうしはぶかにまつようにめいれいしました。) - The supervisor ordered the subordinate to wait.
- コンピューターは命令を実行します。 (コンピューターはめいれいをじっこうします。) - The computer executes instructions.

The second example uses the computing sense: an instruction supplied to a computer.
命令に従う (めいれいにしたがう) means "obey an order," with に marking what is followed.

## How the kanji combine

[命](../kanji/命.md) has a command or mandate meaning as well as its familiar life meaning.
[令](../kanji/令.md) also contributes an order or directive. Their related meanings reinforce the command sense.
The readings are メイ + レイ; this word does not mean "an order about life" in every use.

## Synonyms and antonyms

[頼む](頼む.md) (たのむ), "ask; request," need not assert the authority associated with an order.
[注文](注文.md) (ちゅうもん) is an order for goods or services, a different meaning of English "order."
[従う](従う.md) (したがう) describes complying, not issuing the command.

## Distinctive meaning

Calling an instruction 命令 presents it as a command, not simply helpful advice.
This can matter in describing workplace or personal interactions.
In computing, however, the term is technical rather than a judgment about interpersonal tone.
The recipient and setting distinguish these uses.

Dictionary: [JMdict](https://www.edrdg.org/wiki/index.php/JMdict-EDICT_Dictionary_Project), entry 1532160, senses 1-2.

# 命じる (めいじる) - order; appoint

## Meaning

命じる is a transitive ichidan verb meaning to order or command.
It can also mean to appoint someone to a role.
For an instruction, use **person + に + action + ように命じる** or identify the assigned task with を.

- 部長は私に報告書を出すように命じました。 (ぶちょうはわたしにほうこくしょをだすようにめいじました。) - The department head ordered me to submit a report.
- 私は新しい支店の責任者を命じられました。 (わたしはあたらしいしてんのせきにんしゃをめいじられました。) - I was appointed to take charge of the new branch.

The second example uses the passive **role + を命じられる**.
Conjugations include 命じます, 命じない, 命じた, and 命じて.

## How the kanji combine

[命](../kanji/命.md) contributes a command in this word, not its other meaning "life."
The on-reading stem メイ combines with the Japanese verbal ending じる.
This makes a conjugating verb rather than a noun used unchanged before する.

## Synonyms and antonyms

[命令](命令.md) (めいれい) names an order and forms 命令する.
[頼む](頼む.md) (たのむ) means to ask or request; it need not assert authority.
任命する (にんめいする) explicitly names appointment to a position.

## Distinctive meaning

命じる presents an instruction as a command, not merely advice or a friendly request.
Authority and the assigned responsibility are central to its use.
Do not translate restaurant "ordering" mechanically with 命じる: ordering food is a different sense of English "order."
In the appointment use, the role identifies what responsibility is being assigned.

Dictionary: [JMdict](https://www.edrdg.org/wiki/index.php/JMdict-EDICT_Dictionary_Project), entry 1531950, senses 1-2.

# 命ずる (めいずる) - command; appoint

## Meaning

命ずる is a transitive verb meaning to order or command someone to do something,
or to appoint someone to a post. It is associated with authoritative or formal directions.

- 裁判所は支払いを命じました。 (さいばんしょはしはらいをめいじました。) - The court ordered payment.
- 彼を委員に命じました。 (かれをいいんにめいじました。) - They appointed him to the committee.

In the appointment pattern, 人を役職に命ずる, を marks the person and に marks the post.
The examples use 命じました, a form shared with 命じる.

## How the kanji combine

[命](../kanji/命.md) contributes a command here, not its other meaning "life."
The on reading メイ is followed by ずる.
Japanese dictionaries classify 命ずる as サ変; JMdict uses its "-zuru alternative
of -jiru verbs" category. For the forms used here, learn 命じます (めいじます),
命じた (めいじた), and 命じない (めいじない), not a regular godan ずる pattern.

## Synonyms and antonyms

[命じる](命じる.md) (めいじる) shares the command and appointment meanings.
[命令](命令.md) (めいれい) names an order and can form 命令する.
[指定](指定.md) (してい) can mean designate or specify; specifying a date need not appoint a person.

## Distinctive meaning

The English word "order" also describes a sequence, but 命ずる does not mean putting
things into [順序](順序.md) (じゅんじょ).
Similarly, "command a view" belongs to the view sense of [望む](望む.md) (のぞむ),
not to this verb's command meaning. Shared English wording does not make those Japanese uses interchangeable.
This card covers the pinned entry's command and appointment senses, not every historical use.

Dictionary: [JMdict](https://www.edrdg.org/wiki/index.php/JMdict-EDICT_Dictionary_Project),
entry 1531970, senses 1-2; Japanese classification:
[Digital Daijisen](https://www.weblio.jp/content/命ずる).

# 天皇 (てんのう) - Emperor of Japan

## Meaning

天皇 is the title "Emperor of Japan."
It identifies this particular sovereign's title, rather than any emperor or king in the world.

- 天皇の即位についての記事を読みました。 (てんのうのそくいについてのきじをよみました。) - I read an article about the emperor's accession.
- 天皇陛下が式典に出席されました。 (てんのうへいかがしきてんにしゅっせきされました。) - His Majesty the Emperor attended the ceremony.

天皇陛下 (てんのうへいか) is a respectful form of reference.
The second example uses respectful 出席される for attending.

## How the kanji combine

[天](../kanji/天.md) contributes a heavenly or imperial association, and 皇 "emperor."
Learn the whole reading **てんのう**: the ん before おう produces のう through the sound change
called 連声 (れんじょう), from てんおう. It is not evidence for a general 皇 reading ノウ.
This reading explanation is separate from the historical origin of the title.

## Synonyms and antonyms

皇帝 (こうてい) is the broader title "emperor."
[国王](国王.md) (こくおう) and [王](王.md) (おう) concern a king or monarch;
do not replace an established national title mechanically with one of those words.

## Distinctive meaning

Japanese 天皇 specifically names the Japanese imperial title in the modern use taught here.
English "emperor" alone does not establish that 天皇 is appropriate for a ruler of another country.
The examples teach vocabulary and respectful reference, not a claim about the emperor's political powers.

# 効果 (こうか) - effect; effectiveness

## Meaning

効果 names an effect or the effectiveness of something. It is a noun: 効果がある
means "have an effect; be effective," and 効果がない means "have no effect."
The thing producing the effect can precede の.

- この薬は痛みに効果があります。 (このくすりはいたみにこうかがあります。) - This medicine is effective against pain.
- 広告の効果を調べています。 (こうこくのこうかをしらべています。) - We are investigating the advertisement's effectiveness.

In the medicine example, に marks the condition against which the medicine works.
効果的な (こうかてきな) is the related adjective "effective."

## How the kanji combine

[効](../kanji/効.md) concerns working or having efficacy; [果](../kanji/果.md) contributes a result.
Together they name the result produced by something's action. The readings are
コウ + カ, with a long first vowel.

## Synonyms and antonyms

[結果](結果.md) (けっか) is a result or outcome more generally. 効果 emphasizes
what an action, treatment, or other cause brings about, often in relation to an
intended purpose. An outcome can exist even when an attempted treatment had no
効果.

## Distinctive meaning

The noun does not establish how large or beneficial an effect is. Add a description
or context rather than assuming 効果 means complete success. It also appears in
production terms such as 音響効果 (おんきょうこうか), "sound effects": these are
created effects for a scene, not a statement that the sound is medically effective.

Dictionary: [JMdict](https://www.edrdg.org/wiki/index.php/JMdict-EDICT_Dictionary_Project), entry 1275130, senses 1-2.

# 約束 (やくそく) — promise; agreement

## Meaning

約束 is a promise or agreement that commits someone to something. 約束する means "make a promise."
A verb can describe its content: 会う約束 (あうやくそく), "an agreement to meet."

- 友達と、明日また会う約束をしました。 (ともだちと、あしたまたあうやくそくをしました。) — I promised my friend that we would meet again tomorrow.
- 約束を守ります。 (やくそくをまもります。) — I will keep my promise.

Use person + と for the other party to an agreement. 約束を守る (やくそくをまもる) means to keep a promise;
約束を破る (やくそくをやぶる) means to break one.

## How the kanji combine

[約](../kanji/約.md) contributes the idea of an agreement and [束](../kanji/束.md) that of binding together.
Think of people being bound by an agreement, not of a literal bundle.
The on readings combine as ヤク + ソク.

## Synonyms and antonyms

契約 (けいやく) is a contract or agreement; it is useful when the commitment is a contract.
予約 (よやく) is a reservation or booking, such as securing a restaurant table.
Those ideas can overlap with an arrangement, but a personal promise is not automatically a booking.
[守る](守る.md) (まもる) and [破る](破る.md) (やぶる) provide the practical contrast "keep" versus "break" a promise.

## Distinctive meaning

約束 carries a commitment between people, not just an event that might happen.
約束がある (やくそくがある) can therefore mean that you have an arrangement to meet someone; context supplies the details.
The word does not by itself establish whether the agreement is legally enforceable.

Dictionary: [JMdict](https://www.edrdg.org/wiki/index.php/JMdict-EDICT_Dictionary_Project), entry 1538130, sense 1.
Comparisons and combinations: entries 1250190, 1543750, 1327120 (sense 2), and 1471200 (sense 5).

# 法律 (ほうりつ) — law; legislation

## Meaning

法律 means law or legislation: legally established rules, or a particular law understood from context. It can also name law as a subject of study.

大学で法律を勉強しています。 (だいがくでほうりつをべんきょうしています。) — I am studying law at university.

## How the kanji combine

[法](../kanji/法.md) and [律](../kanji/律.md) both contribute rule or law meanings. The on readings ほう + りつ form ほうりつ. Preserve the long vowel in ほう.

## Synonyms and antonyms

規則 (きそく) means rules or regulations, including those of a school or workplace. ルール is a broader everyday loanword. 法律 specifically concerns law rather than every informal rule.

## Distinctive meaning

法律を守る (ほうりつをまもる) means obeying the law; 法律に違反する (ほうりつにいはんする) means violating it. Note the different particles. The word itself does not mean a lawyer: that profession is 弁護士 (べんごし).

Dictionary: [JMdict](https://www.edrdg.org/wiki/index.php/JMdict-EDICT_Dictionary_Project), entry 1517480, sense 1.

# 規則 (きそく) — rules and regulations

## Meaning

規則 means a rule or set of regulations, such as those of a school, workplace, or activity. Japanese does not require a plural ending when several rules are meant.

学校の規則を守ってください。 (がっこうのきそくをまもってください。) — Please follow the school rules.

## How the kanji combine

[規](../kanji/規.md) suggests a standard or rule, and [則](../kanji/則.md) also means a rule or principle. Their on readings combine as キ + ソク. Together they name the rules that govern conduct or a procedure.

## Synonyms and antonyms

ルール is an everyday loanword for "rule." 法律 (ほうりつ) means law, not merely any organization's rule. 約束 (やくそく) is a promise or arrangement between people.

## Distinctive meaning

Learn 規則 with its verbs: 規則を守る (きそくをまもる), "obey the rules," and 規則を破る (きそくをやぶる), "break the rules." 規則 itself is a noun, not the adjective "regular."

Source: [JMdict](https://www.edrdg.org/jmdict/j_jmdict.html), entry 1223021, sense 1.

# 法 (ほう) - law; method

## Meaning

法 is a noun for law or a principle. As a suffix, ～法 appears in the names of laws or acts.
It also has a method sense, so a word ending in 法 is not necessarily the name of a statute.

- 私たちは法を守らなければなりません。 (わたしたちはほうをまもらなければなりません。) - We must obey the law.
- 自分に合う勉強法を探しています。 (じぶんにあうべんきょうほうをさがしています。) - I am looking for a study method that suits me.

For the legal suffix, 道路交通法 (どうろこうつうほう), "Road Traffic Act," is a concrete example.
In 勉強法, by contrast, 法 means a way of studying.

## How the kanji combine

The single character [法](../kanji/法.md) supplies the complete word, using the on reading ホウ.
Within a compound, preceding material identifies what law or method is meant.
Do not translate each occurrence as "Act" without checking the whole expression.

## Synonyms and antonyms

[法律](法律.md) (ほうりつ) explicitly names law or laws.
[方法](方法.md) (ほうほう), "method," is a useful comparison for the nonlegal sense.
These are two related areas of meaning, not interchangeable replacements in every compound.

## Distinctive meaning

Learn 法 both as a standalone noun and as an element in longer words.
The source-list gloss "Act" points to the legal naming use, which this card teaches explicitly.
The broader word also supports method expressions; those do not describe legally required behavior.
There is no single opposite covering both uses.

Dictionary: [JMdict](https://www.edrdg.org/wiki/index.php/JMdict-EDICT_Dictionary_Project), entry 1517150, senses 1-2.

# 人 — person

**Strokes:** 2 · **Key (radical):** 人 (no. 9; as a left-hand component 亻, にんべん) · **JLPT:** N5 (community list)

## Meaning and origin

人 is a pictograph of a person seen from the side: a body with an arm or leg leaning forward. Compare [大](大.md), a
frontal figure with arms spread. As 亻 on the left it marks people and human activity: 休 ([休](休.md)), 住, 作, 体, 何, 他.

Because 人 and 入 ([入](入.md)) are nearly mirror images, they are a classic confusion. In 人 the long left-falling stroke is written first from the top and
the right-falling stroke starts from its middle; in 入 the short left-falling stroke comes first and the long right-falling stroke starts at the top, to its upper left.

## Readings

| Reading | Type | Typical words |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ジン | on | [人口](../words/人口.md) じんこう, 日本人 にほんじん, 外国人 がいこくじん |
| ニン | on | 人間 にんげん, 三人 さんにん, 人気 にんき, 職人 しょくにん |
| ひと | kun | 人 ひと, 女の人 おんなのひと, 人々 ひとびと |
| -り | kun | counting one and two persons: 一人 ひとり, 二人 ふたり (special forms) |

Special reading: [大人](../words/大人.md) おとな (adult).

## Common words

- [人口](../words/人口.md) じんこう — population
- [大人](../words/大人.md) おとな — adult
- 人 ひと — person, people

## Notes

人々 ひとびと (people) repeats the kanji with the repetition mark 々 and voices the second ひと.

# 何 — what

**Strokes:** 7 · **Key (radical):** 人 (as 亻, no. 9) · **Phonetic:** 可 (カ) · **JLPT:** N5 (community list)

## Meaning and origin

何 is a phonetic compound: 亻 ([人](人.md), person) and 可 (カ, "can, possible"). In classical Chinese it was an interrogative "what?", "which?",
and the original sense "carry" (later written 荷) is commonly cited for the character. How the "what" use arose from it is not firmly settled, so treat the history as debated.
In Japanese it is the basic question word "what", used also for "how many" before counters.

## Readings

| Reading | Type | Typical words |
| --- | --- | --- |
| カ | on | 幾何 きか (geometry), rare in everyday words |
| なに | kun | 何 なに, [何か](../words/何か.md) なにか, 何も なにも, 何色 なにいろ, 何人 なにじん (what nationality) |
| なん | kun | [何時](../words/何時.md) なんじ, [何人](../words/何人.md) なんにん, 何分 なんぷん, 何歳 なんさい, 何年 なんねん |

## Common words

- [何時](../words/何時.md) なんじ — what time
- [何人](../words/何人.md) なんにん — how many people
- [何か](../words/何か.md) なにか — something

## Notes

- **なに vs なん:** 何 is read なん before the sounds t, d, n (なんでも, なんだ, なんの) and before most counters (何時, 何人, 何分); otherwise なに (何を, 何が, 何か). This is a tendency with exceptions, so learn common words as units.
- 何人 is なんにん "how many people" but なにじん "what nationality".
- Look-alike: 河 (river) and 荷 (load) share the 可 component; 何 has 亻 on the left, and is not [今](今.md).

# 入 — enter, put in

**Strokes:** 2 · **Key (radical):** 入 (no. 11) · **JLPT:** N5 (community list)

## Meaning and origin

入 is often described as a pictograph of something pointed going inward (an entrance or tip), but the origin is debated.
Use it as a mnemonic: two strokes converging, opposite to the outward 出 ([出](出.md)).
It means "enter", "go in" and "put in".

It looks like 人 ([人](人.md)) but the strokes differ: the short left-falling stroke is written first, then the long right-falling stroke from the top (人 is the other way round).

# 女 — woman, female

**Strokes:** 3 · **Key (radical):** 女 (no. 38) · **JLPT:** N5 (community list)

## Meaning and origin

女 is a pictograph of a kneeling figure with crossed hands. As a key it appears in many kanji about women and family: 母, 姉, 妹, 好, 姫, 嫁.
In 好 (like), 女 and 子 (child) are commonly explained as mother and child. Component meanings are a historical layer, not a description of the word today.

## Readings

| Reading | Type | Typical words |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ジョ | on | [男女](../words/男女.md) だんじょ, 女性 じょせい, 彼女 かのじょ, 少女 しょうじょ |
| ニョ | on | 老若男女 ろうにゃくなんにょ |
| ニョウ | on | 女房 にょうぼう |
| おんな | kun | 女 おんな, 女の子 おんなのこ, 女の人 おんなのひと |
| め | kun | 女神 めがみ, 女滝 めだき |

## Common words

- [男女](../words/男女.md) だんじょ — men and women
- 女性 じょせい — female (formal/polite)
- 女の子 おんなのこ — girl

## Notes

Opposite: [男](男.md). 女 can read おんな or め; 女の子 is the everyday word for "girl".

**Stroke-order mnemonic: くノ一.** The three strokes of 女, in order, look like the characters く, ノ and 一. Japanese fiction uses this as the word くノ一 (くのいち, "kunoichi"), now popularly "female ninja". The word is a playful spelling of 女 itself; it was a slang term for "woman" in the Edo period, and its "female ninja" meaning was popularised by novelist Yamada Fūtarō in the 1960s. Historians have found no records of female ninja working exactly like the men, so treat the image as a memory aid and pop-culture word, not as history. The first stroke (く) has the bend; then the long diagonal (ノ); the horizontal (一) comes last and crosses both.

# 日 — sun, day

**Strokes:** 4 · **Key (radical):** 日 (no. 72) · **Phonetic:** none (not a phonetic compound) · **JLPT:** N5 (community list)

## Meaning and origin

日 is a pictograph of the sun. The oldest forms are round, often with a dot or short line inside; brush and carving
styles squared the circle. What the inner mark originally represented is uncertain, so treat any story about it
(a sunspot, a core) as a mnemonic rather than established fact.

The same word covers both "the sun" and "a day" (one sun-cycle), which is why one character serves for both
and for the days of the week and the month (日曜日, 十日). As a component, 日 usually hints at the sun, daylight or time,
as in 明 (日 + 月, bright), 時, 晴, 昨.

It is easy to confuse with 目 (eye, taller with two inner lines), 白 (white, one extra stroke on top) and [月](月.md) (moon, slimmer, with two inner strokes).

## Readings

| Reading | Type | Typical words |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ニチ | on | 日曜日 にちようび, 毎日 まいにち, 日本 にほん／にっぽん, 日記 にっき |
| ジツ | on | [休日](../words/休日.md) きゅうじつ, 平日 へいじつ, 祝日 しゅくじつ, 先日 せんじつ |
| ひ | kun | 日 ひ (sun, day), 日の出 ひので, 日当たり ひあたり |
| -び | kun | 誕生日 たんじょうび, 記念日 きねんび (voiced form of ひ in compounds) |
| -か | kun | day counting: 二日 ふつか, 三日 みっか, 十日 とおか; 一日 ついたち is special |

Special readings: 今日 きょう, 昨日 きのう, 明日 あした／あす.

## Common words

- [日中](../words/日中.md) にっちゅう — daytime; also Japan–China (日中関係)
- [月日](../words/月日.md) つきひ／がっぴ — time passing; calendar date
- [休日](../words/休日.md) きゅうじつ — day off, holiday
- 毎日 まいにち — every day
- [日本刀](../words/日本刀.md) にほんとう — Japanese sword; 日本 names Japan in this compound

## Notes

The five-element kanji [火](火.md) [水](水.md) [木](木.md) (plus 金 土) combine with 日 and [月](月.md) in the weekday names:
日曜日, 月曜日, 火曜日, 水曜日, 木曜日, 金曜日, 土曜日.

# 月 — moon, month

**Strokes:** 4 · **Key (radical):** 月 (no. 74) · **JLPT:** N5 (community list)

## Meaning and origin

月 is a pictograph of a crescent moon. Old forms show the crescent with a mark inside it, usually explained as
shading on the moon or a way to tell it apart from 夕 (evening), which historically descends from the same picture.
Like 日 ([日](日.md)), it serves for both a celestial body and the time unit it measures: a lunar cycle gives "month", and
つき is both "moon" and "month" in Japanese.

Two things to keep apart:

- In 明 (bright) it is really the moon, paired with the sun: 日 + 月.
- In many body-part kanji (e.g. 腕, 脳) the 月 on the left is not the moon but the flesh radical 肉 (にくづき), which
  has a similar shape in modern print.

## Readings

| Reading | Type | Typical words |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ゲツ | on | 月曜日 げつようび, 今月 こんげつ, 来月 らいげつ |
| ガツ | on | month names: 一月 いちがつ, 十二月 じゅうにがつ; 正月 しょうがつ |
| つき | kun | 月 つき (moon, month), 月日 つきひ, 三日月 みかづき (voiced and shortened) |

ガツ is used for the numbered month names (一月–十二月); ゲツ for "month" as a counted span (一ヶ月 いっかげつ) and the weekday.

## Common words

- [月日](../words/月日.md) つきひ／がっぴ — time passing; calendar date
- 月曜日 げつようび — Monday
- 毎月 まいつき／まいげつ — every month (both readings are used)

## Notes

For the weekday series see [日](日.md); 月 pairs with [日](日.md) as the "sun and moon" of 日月.

# 男 — man, male

**Strokes:** 7 · **Key (radical):** 田 (no. 102) · **Phonetic:** none (an ideographic compound) · **JLPT:** N5 (community list)

## Meaning and origin

男 combines 田 (rice field) and 力 (strength, often explained as a plough or an arm). The traditional reading is "someone who
works the field with strength", reflecting a historical picture of male labour.
It is a compound ideogram: both parts contribute meaning, neither contributes sound.

## Readings

| Reading | Type | Typical words |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ダン | on | [男女](../words/男女.md) だんじょ, 男性 だんせい, 男子 だんし |
| ナン | on | 長男 ちょうなん, 次男 じなん, 老若男女 ろうにゃくなんにょ |
| おとこ | kun | 男 おとこ, 男の子 おとこのこ, 男前 おとこまえ |
| お | kun | rare, e.g. 男滝 おだき (the male waterfall of a pair) |

## Common words

- [男女](../words/男女.md) だんじょ — men and women
- 男性 だんせい — male (formal/polite)
- 男の子 おとこのこ — boy

## Notes

Opposite: [女](女.md). Pairing order in kango is 男女, not 女男.

# 買 — buy

**Strokes:** 12 · **Key (radical):** 貝 (shell, no. 154) · **JLPT:** N4 (community list)

## Meaning and origin

買 is commonly explained as 罒 (a net, a form of 网) over 貝 (a shell): shells were an early form of money, so the picture
is of "gathering in" goods with money. As the details of the early forms are debated, take the net image as a mnemonic.
The key 貝 appears in many money and trade words: 財, 貯 and 貨. (売 looks similar but has no 貝 in its modern form; its radical is 士.)

## Readings

| Reading | Type | Typical words |
| --- | --- | --- |
| バイ | on | 売買 ばいばい (buying and selling), 購買 こうばい, 買収 ばいしゅう |
| か.う | kun | [買う](../words/買う.md) かう, [買い物](../words/買い物.md) かいもの, 買い方 かいかた |

## Common words

- [買う](../words/買う.md) かう — to buy
- [買い物](../words/買い物.md) かいもの — shopping
- 買い手 かいて — buyer

## Notes

- Opposite: 売る うる (sell), written 売; the two kanji look alike at a glance, but 買 has 罒 over 貝 while 売 has 士 over a different base. かう is also 飼う (keep an animal), a homophone with another spelling.
- Look-alikes: [見](見.md) (see) is 目 over 儿 (legs); 買 has 罒 over 貝, and 貝 itself contains 目 over 八. 貝 is also a part of 貸 (lend) and 貯.
- 買う is a regular godan verb: 買います, 買わない (note the わ, not あ), 買って, 買った.
